raw_response:
C13 — Baseline B

I found three transferable candidates. The application statements below are translations by an internal model, not results of a human study or evidence of deployment.

1. Jep (Java Embedded Python)
   Primary source: https://github.com/ninia/jep
   Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/uhub/awesome-c
   Its managed wrapper around embedded CPython subinterpreters could inform a Python-facing interface to the existing interpreter capability. The host API is Java/JNI, and the README describes only partial isolation.
   Date status: unknown. The live README is undated; a separately opened dated comparison page is not used as clean evidence because of an unresolved adjacent-proposal reference.

2. Lupa — separate LuaRuntime objects
   Primary source: https://github.com/scoder/lupa
   Discovery catalogue: https://github.com/alirezabayatmk/awesome-python-1
   Its Python objects for separate runtime states could inform interpreter handles and explicit transfer between isolated execution contexts. The documentation requires copying or explicit communication between runtimes. Lua differs from CPython, so this is an API and ownership analogy.
   Date status: unknown. The live README does not establish historical availability of the described behavior.

3. Enterprise Integration Patterns — Message Channel
   Primary source: https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/MessageChannel.html
   Discovery catalogue: https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/toc.html
   A channel with explicit writers and readers could inform controlled data exchange without granting direct access to another interpreter's state. This application-integration pattern does not specify CPython payload ownership, blocking or teardown.
   Date status: unknown. No dated original edition was opened.

These are partial design inputs. None establishes the complete requested standard-library interface, and no parallel speedup requirement is assumed. Search output included off-catalogue snippets; their exposures are recorded separately from the opened catalogue listings and primary verification.

budget.counting_method: Conservative: every open, click and find page retrieval counts, including repeat views and the failed fetch; search-result snippets are not page opens.

limitations: Only the assigned baseline rules and C13 prefix were read locally; no gold, other prefixes/runs, judgments, repository history or target document was read.

The first searches used broad awesome-list keywords rather than precise catalogue paths. Both search engines also returned off-catalogue results for later inurl-restricted queries. These snippets were visible and cannot be erased; relevant exposures are recorded.

Jep and Lupa names and descriptions appeared in off-catalogue snippets before their catalogue entries were inspected. No primary candidate page was opened before an opened permitted catalogue listing identified it.
Only candidates independently identified in opened permitted catalogues were retained. Primary pages were used only to verify those candidates, not to discover additional candidates.
One raw catalogue fetch failed with DisabledError; there was no attempt to bypass that restriction.

The dated Jep comparison page was excluded as uncertain adjacent-proposal exposure. The Lupa changelog returned no dated body. All retained candidates therefore have date_status unknown; post_decision false does not assert pre-cutoff availability.
Current awesome-list membership is not proof that an entry was present at the cutoff.
This was an internal separate-context GPT-6 Astra Pro run, not a human study or a different-model control. Model pretraining memory is not controlled.
The page budget was reached using the conservative retrieval count; no further date-verification page was opened.
